newsitem.title: UK: Queens Moat gets 8.5 mln stg for Bath hotel.
newsitem.headline: Queens Moat gets 8.5 mln stg for Bath hotel.

text.p: Queens Moat Houses Plc said on Friday it had exchanged contracts for the sale of its luxury The Royal Crescent Hotel in Bath to Cliveden Plc for 8.5 million stg.
Queens Moat, which recently put up a portfolio of 25 hotels for sale, said it would use the proceeds mainly to reduce its debt, with the balance being used to fund working capital.

In a separate statement, luxury hotel group Cliveden said it would pay for the hotel with 4.5 million stg from existing cash resources and 4.0 million stg which will be funded by a new medium-term bank loan.
The sale is expected to be completed on November 5.
Queens Moat said the Royal Crescent was currently valued at 8.5 million stg on an open market basis, up from 6.0 million stg at end 1995.

The company said the increase was due to a number of factors, including the improved market for hotel transactions, the hotel's improved trading performance, and the potential development of an adjacent property that was not included in the December 1995 valuation.
The hotel made a trading profit of 635,000 stg in 1995.
Cliveden said last month it was in talks to buy the Royal Crescent, which is located in Bath's Georgian district.
